To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) uploading-only peers were the majority, smooth-watching peers the majority of them, in the measured P2P VoDs; (2) the relations between WI distributions and network-sharing profiles were established; and (3) a mathematical model was established, and validated by the measured data, to analytically explain the relations between WI distribution and network-sharing profiles.
the current P2V VoD systems show different characteristics from the existing file dissemination systems.
the current P2VOD system is more like a file dissemination system rather than a VoD system, and the WI distribution is the most critical factor that determines the network-sharing profile.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characteristics of P-to-P VoD systems and the relation between users watching behavior and network-sharing profile.
the characteristics of P-to-P VoD systems, and the results obtained from this study will be useful in the future development of P2P-based VoD systems.
the practical P2P VoDs and the measured results will be useful to the system designers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
smooth-watching peers are more selfish than randomly-seeking peers, which is the opposite to that of file dissemination.
smooth-watching peers are more likely to share the rarest chunks, while randomly-seeking peers tend to upload the regular chunks.
the network-sharing profile is not a simple reflection of the watching behavior of peers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in P2P-based systems, peers with different watching behavior will contribute to network differently.
the watching behavior is a critical factor in the network sharing of the P2P VoDs, and the WI distribution can be used to predict the network-sharing profile.
the WI distribution can be used as the key metric to characterize the network sharing in P 2P VoD system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the network sharing of P2P-based VoD systems can be improved by increasing the ratio of randomly-seeking peers.
the network-sharing profiles of P2P-based VoD systems are different from those of other P2P systems and that this difference should be taken into account when designing a new P2P-based video service.
the watching behavior has a significant impact on the network sharing profile in P2P-based VoD systems.
